thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: Elevated 5xx error rate on /v1/generate (us-west1) — threshold breached (5m). Triggered by service: inference-runtime. Priority: P1.
Alex: I’m on it. Seeing a big spike in gateway 502/504 from the model-runtime pool.
Jia: Confirming — Grafana dashboards show a sharp increase starting ~T-7m. Latency also up ~3x.
Samir: Any customer reports? CS thread shows a few requests failing with 502s, some timeouts.
pagerduty-bot: Incident channel created: #incidents.6831234567. On-call: alex. Next: jia.
Maria: @alex @jia I’ve forwarded initial customer errors to legal/CS. No outage page yet but some users are in prod.
Alex: Quick triage: tailing runtime logs on a handful of affected hosts. Seeing repeated segfaults in model-runner:

```
2026-03-15T10:12:02Z model-runner[pid=1432]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f8a3eee kernel_module
backtrace: ...
```
Also OOM-related liveness restarts on two nodes.
Jia: Which variant? Looks like model xlarge-17b-quant from the logs. Could be quant attention kernel bug.
Samir: Trying to repro on a staging node with same model and request shape. If it's kernel-specific we should reroute traffic to a different variant (xlarge-17b-fp16) and scale capacity.
Leo: I’ll flip routing policy to favor fp16 variant for us-west1 canary first. Preparing a temporary route rule: `route: if region==us-west1 -> prefer model:xlarge-17b-fp16 fallback:model:xlarge-17b-quant`.
ops-bot: Running `redwood route update --region us-west1 --policy prefer-fp16 --dry-run` -> no conflicts.
Alex: Good. Also mark affected nodes as unschedulable so autoscaler can provision replacements. Offloading existing work will help.
Jia: Repro on staging succeeded: the quant kernel crashes when requests have prefix length > 1024. It’s likely a KV cache boundary bug causing pointer corruption.
Samir: Can we enable prefix/KV cache bypass for that model as a mitigation? That would reduce efficiency but avoid crash.
Alex: Yes. Probe config: set `kvcache.enabled=false` for xlarge-17b-quant in us-west1 via dynamic config. Doing that now.
ops-bot: Applying dynamic config patch: `{\n  "model": "xlarge-17b-quant",\n  "region": "us-west1",\n  "kvcache.enabled": "false"\n}` -> applied to pool `us-west1-quant-1`
Maria: Noting customer impact: CS reports ~12 customers experienced intermittent failures; two customers on high-throughput plans saw sustained errors. Escalated to account managers.
product-ops: We should consider temporary rollback to an older quantized kernel build if this persists. Documenting.
Alex: Observability: enabling debug-level coredumps for the runner and increasing sampling on stack traces. Also enabling extra metrics for per-model segfault counts.
eng-sre-bot: New metric `model_segfault_count{model=\"xlarge-17b-quant\",region=\"us-west1\"}` is incrementing. Current value: 18 in last 5m.
Leo: Route update completed. Traffic to xlarge-17b-quant in us-west1 reduced by ~85% in the last 3m. Error rate on gateway now dropping.
Jia: Staging patch: add bounds check around kv pointer in `attention_kernels.c`. Running CI hotfix build.
Samir: While CI finishes, we should scale up fp16 capacity in us-west1 to handle diverted load. Requesting +10 GPUs from autoscaler.
ops-bot: Autoscaler request accepted; provisioning 8 GPUs initially across two nodes. ETA ~4m.
Alex: Running a temporary global fallback for customers on SLAs: `fallback.policy=always_use_fp16_for_high_priority` so SLA traffic doesn't hit the quant path.
Maria: CS will send an update to affected customers listing mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery. Draft ready, waiting for timeline confirmation.
Alex: Monitoring: 502 rate down 60% since reroute. Latency dropping back to normal for most requests. Two hosts still flapping with restarts — isolating them for postmortem.
Jia: CI hotfix passed unit + integration tests; packaging a hotpatch. Planning a canary deploy to a single quant node with additional sanitizers.
Leo: Canary deploy scheduled on `us-west1-quant-canary-1`. Will watch for segfaults for 10m.
eng-sre-bot: Canary metrics: 0 segfaults in first 6m, memory profile stable.
Samir: Good sign. If canary stays clean for 10m, we can roll the patch to remaining quant nodes.
Alex: For now incident classification: P1 (customer impact, elevated 5xx). Mitigation in place: routing + kvcache bypass + autoscale + patch rollout.
Maria: CS update sent: "We’ve implemented routing mitigations and are deploying a fix; services are recovering. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary."
product-ops: Please add an action item to test quant kernels against long-prefix workloads during onboarding.
Alex: Action items logged: 1) Postmortem ownership (Jia) 2) Kernel regression test addition (Samir) 3) Customer RCA and timeline (Maria) 4) Node remediation checklist (Leo).
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged -> status: mitigation in progress. If no re-escalation in 30m, we’ll de-escalate to P2 monitoring.
Alex: I’ll keep this channel open. Shout if anything spikes back up. Great work everyone. :heart:
